uncited: Diffuse Lighting Models compute the illumination of surfaces defined by Signed Distance Fields (SDFs) or meshes by estimating surface normals and applying reflectance models to determine how light interacts with the geometry.
They solve the problem of shading ray-marched or rasterized geometry without explicit mesh topology (for SDFs) or to smooth faceted appearances (for meshes).

This family is distinguished from [Distance Color Blending](791-distance-color-blending.md) by explicitly calculating geometric lighting contributions (diffuse/specular) rather than relying solely on distance-based color mapping, and from [Ray-marched Shadows](1087-ray-marched-shadows.md) by focusing on the local reflectance properties rather than global occlusion calculations.

Phong shading, while not explicitly detailed in the provided SDF-specific notes, is a standard extension of these models that interpolates normals rather than colors, providing more accurate specular highlights.
